analysis: Examined ProviderLoop+Serve.swift (head, lines 1-603) and ProviderLoop+Testing.swift (patch plus base). The security-relevant change is in the serve loop's work consumer. Line 300 makes non-order-free events call awaitReleasedAdmissions() before they are processed. Lines 329-348 wrap handleInferenceRequest in admitInWorkFIFO, passing a gate. The same parameters are forwarded, including authenticatedCacheScope: cacheScope, so the coordinator-authored cache scope plumbing relevant to T-041 is unchanged. Line 351 adds deferCancelForReleasedAdmission before handleCancellation, and line 397 awaits released admissions at consumer end. This appears to preserve ordering. Cancel is deferred rather than dropped, and disconnect or other events wait for released admissions, so cleanup (cancelAllInflight on .disconnected) should not be reordered ahead of a request admitted earlier. Connection-control events (.appAttestShadow, .trustStatus, connected/disconnected invalidation) remain on the separate eventTask reader (lines 405-419). This preserves the earlier App Attest dispatch-availability property, and clearConnectionAuthorization is still called synchronously. The Testing.swift changes are only test seams that set coldLoadReleasesWorkFIFO and read releasedAdmissions.count; they are internal and not production-reachable. Remaining questions are outside the supplied evidence. ProviderLoop+WorkFIFO.swift (admitInWorkFIFO, awaitReleasedAdmissions, deferCancelForReleasedAdmission, overtakesReleasedAdmissions) and the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE init were not supplied. Integration should check that a released admission cannot let a request run past a disconnect or revocation. It should also check that a request admitted after a session change still validates the current connection authorization (T-053), that the in-flight registration for a released cold-load request is cancelled on disconnect, and that bounded queueing cannot cause unbounded memory growth or a stall (T-010, availability).
